COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, UMESH M.ADIGA J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -5-  MFA No. 101712 of 2015  MFA.CROB No. 100166 of 2016
JUDGMENT
This appeal arises out of the judgment and award dated 18.03.2015 passed in MVC No.1530/2012 by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Belagavi.
Respondent No.2 in MVC No.1530/2012 has filed this appeal challenging the impugned judgment on ground of its liability to pay the compensation so also quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
During pendency of this appeal, claimants have also filed cross objection challenging the impugned judgment and claiming enhancement of the compensation in MFA Crob.100166/2016.
Therefore, both the matters are taken up together for disposal.
2. We refer the parties as per their rank before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.

3. It was the case of petitioner respondent No.1 herein that, on 25.04.2012 at about 9.45 p.m. her husband Babu Laxman Muntelkar @ Satarkar @ Warandekar was going in a motorcycle bearing No.KA-30/R-1210 as a pillion rider from Londa towards Ramnagar.
The deceased Vinod Pandurang Shirsat was the rider of the motorcycle.

When the said vehicle came near Londa-Durga bridge, rider of the motorcycle was riding his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner; He suddenly saw a vehicle coming from the opposite direction lost control over his motorcycle and went to the wrong side of the road.
As a consequences, he dashed motorcycle against the vehicle coming from opposite direction.
Due to the impact, the said Vinod died at the spot and Babu Laxman Muntelkar had sustained grievous injuries.
People tried to shift Babu to the hospital and on the way, he succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident.
4. It was the further case of the petitioners before the Tribunal that the deceased was aged about 25 years at the time of the accident, he was driver by profession and earning Rs.10,000/- as salary.
Petitioner was widow, respondent Nos.3 and 4 were parents of the deceased, were entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
With these reasons, they have claimed compensation of Rs.13,65,000/-.
5. Owner of the motorcycle had not appeared before the Tribunal.
The appellant-respondent No.2 has contended before the Tribunal that the accident had taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of an unidentified vehicle by its driver.
The complaint was filed in the police station regarding the said unidentified vehicle.
Rider of the motorcycle was not charge sheeted by the police.
The FIR and charge sheet filed by the police was against the unidentified vehicle and not against the deceased Vinod.

Therefore, respondent No.2 is not at all concerned with the said The Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160201200/
5 accident and it is not liable to pay the compensation.

entities.text: Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further contended by respondent No.2 before the Tribunal that the said Vinod was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said motorcycle as on the date of the alleged accident and owner of the said vehicle had violated conditions of the policy.
Therefore, respondent No.2 is exonerated from liability to pay the compensation to the claimants.
6. The Tribunal on the basis of the contention of both the parties framed necessary issues.
7. Claimant has examined as P.W.1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P12.

Respondent No.2 examined R.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.R1 to 3.
8.

Being aggrieved by the said findings of the Tribunal, this appeal is filed by respondent No.2.
10.
We have heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the cross objectors.

11. Following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether appellant/respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation as contended?
ii) Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of the compensation?
iii) What order?
12.
Learned counsel for the appellant vehemently contended that according to the case of prosecution, the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of an unidentified vehicle.
Accordingly, 'C' report was filed.
The rider of the motorcycle was not at all responsible for the accident.
However, the Tribunal fastened the liability on respondent No.2 i.e., the appellant to pay the compensation, which is erroneous.

Moreover, the rider of the motorcycle was not holding valid The Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160201200/
6 and effective driving licence to ride the motorcycle and he had only - 10 - learner's licence.

entities.text: The Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the contrary, deceased pillion rider had also no licence to ride two wheeler.
Hence, the requirement of Central Motor Vehicle Act was not complied and hence, it is breach of condition of the policy of insurance by the owner of the motorcycle.
Hence, appellant is not liable to pay the compensation.
The learned counsel for the appellant further contended that amount of compensation awarded is highly excessive.
He has contended that the Tribunal has taken the earnings of the deceased as Rs.7,000/- p.m. without any basis.

The contention of respondent No.2 that the deceased was driver of a lorry, but according to the licence held by him, he was holding the licence to drive LMV and hence, the contention of the claimant do not supported by documents produced by her.
13. The Tribunal ought to have taken income of the deceased as Rs.6,500/-p.m. as per the schedule of income considered for settling the matters before the Lok Adalath.

The Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased on the basis of notional income and hence, it was appropriate to consider 40% of his income to be added towards future prospects instead of - 11 - 50% that has taken by the Tribunal.
Therefore, prayed for re- calculate the same.
It is also submitted that the amount of compensation awarded under other heads are also excessive.
With these reasons prayed to dismissal of petition.
14. Learned counsel for respondent No.1 has vehemently contended that earning of the deceased was Rs.10,000/- p.m. since he was a skilled labour.
The Tribunal has not considered the same.
The Tribunal has not awarded suitable amount of compensation under other heads.
Therefore, prayed for enhancement of the compensation.
15. The Tribunal has taken the age of the deceased as 25 years and suitable multiplier applicable to the case is '18' and income of the deceased as Rs.7,000/- p.m.

it is also added 50% of the income towards future prospects and deducted 1/3rd of the said income towards personal expenses of the deceased and accordingly calculated the amount of compensation under the head loss of dependency.
16. As rightly submitted by learned counsel for the appellant, the income taken by the Tribunal is on the higher - 12 - side.

While deciding the matter or settling the matters before the Lok Adalath, table of notional income is prepared and according to the said table, if any accident had taken place during 2012,
notional income of the victim or deceased who died in the accident, is taken as Rs.6,500/- p.m. and The Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160201200/

entities.text: Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7 the same is to be taken in the present case.
The deceased had no fixed income.
Therefore, 40% of the said income has to be added towards future prospects and as rightly held by the Tribunal 1/3rd of the said amount is to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Suitable multiplier applicable in the present case is '18'.

According to the said calculation, the amount of compensation for which the petitioners as well as respondent Nos.3 and 4 were entitled under the head loss of dependency is Rs.6,067/- x 12 x 18 = Rs.13,10,472/-.
17.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 1National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others and in the case of 2Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 (2018 SCC Online SC 1546)

entities.text: 1National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
2Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 (2018 SCC Online SC 1546)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: - 13 - Ram, and in the case of N.Jayasree and Others vs. Cholamandalam
Ms General Insurance Company Ltd.
Reported in AIR 2021 SC 5218, Rs.44,000/- is to be awarded towards loss of consortium.
In this case, dependents of the deceased were his wife and parents.
However, during the pendency of the petition, father had died.
Therefore, wife and mother are entitled for compensation under the head loss of consortium.
Accordingly, they are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each towards spousal consortium as well as parental consortium.

As per the law laid down in the above said judgments,
Rs.16,500/- each is to be awarded towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Thus, the claimants are entitled for following amount of compensation:
 Sl. No. Heads Amount (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 13,10,472  2. Loss of consortium 88,000  3. Loss of estate 16,500  4.
Funeral expenses 16,500

Accordingly, the petitioners in all are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,31,472/- as against Rs.16,37,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

8 19.

entities.text: Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal relying on the judgments referred by both the parties, which were mentioned in the impugned judgment, has come to the conclusion that even though the charge sheet was filed against an unidentified vehicle, but the accident had taken place due to collusion between the two vehicles and there might be contributory or composite negligence of driver of both the vehicles.

Therefore,
the claimants can claim compensation from any one of the joint tort-feaser.
Accordingly, the petition was maintainable and respondent No.2 i.e., appellant was liable to pay the compensation.

The Tribunal relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2014 ACC 386 in the case of Pavan Kumar and Another Vs Harikrishan Dass Mohanlal and Others and held that even though the charge sheet was filed against an unidentified driver of the vehicle or unidentified vehicle, respondent No.2 was liable to pay the (2014) I ACC 386 (SC)
- 15 - compensation as the said vehicle was also involved in the accident.

entities.text: Pavan Kumar and Another Vs Harikrishan Dass Mohanlal and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said finding is on the basis of law laid down by the superior courts and hence, does not call for any interference.
There is no contrary judgment subsequent to the judgment in the case of Pavankumar and Others (supra).
Therefore, it has a judicial precedent to be followed by the subordinate courts to the Supreme Court.

Hence, the contention of the appellant that the case was registered against an unidentified vehicle,
therefore, appellant is not liable to pay the compensation does not merit consideration.

20. It was also contended by the learned counsel for the appellant that deceased rider of the motorcycle had learner's licence to ride the vehicle and he had not complied strict provisions of Central Motor Vehicles Act and on that count also, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
The said contention is also not sustainable.
Detailed discussions were already made by the Tribunal in the impugned judgment, which holds water and it does not call for any interference.
If rider of the motorcycle had only learner's licence and admittedly, the deceased Babu was a pillion rider had licence to - 16 - drive the light motor vehicle.
The requirement of law is, the person who was sitting as a pillion rider must know the art of driving, so that he can guide the rider of the vehicle.
Admittedly, the deceased had valid driving licence, therefore, it is sufficient compliance of the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act and Rules.
Hence, on that basis also, the appellant cannot disown its liability to pay the compensation.

21. For the aforesaid discussions, we answer the above points accordingly and we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER MFA No.101712/2015 is partly allowed and MFA Cro.100166/2016 is dismissed.
The impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.1530/2012 dated 18.03.2015 is modified.

Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are directed to pay compensation of The Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160201200/
9 Rs.14,31,472/- as against Rs.16,37,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
As rightly held by the Tribunal, petitioners are entitled for interest on the said compensation amount at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of the entire amount.
The remaining portion of the impugned  judgment is kept intact.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The appellant-respondent No.2 has contended before the Tribunal that the accident had taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of an unidentified vehicle by its driver.
Rider of the motorcycle was not charge sheeted by the police.
opennyai_summary.issue:
11. Following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether appellant/respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation as contended?
ii) Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of the compensation?
iii) What order?
12.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The rider of the motorcycle was not at all responsible for the accident.
Moreover, the rider of the motorcycle was not holding valid The Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160201200/
6 and effective driving licence to ride the motorcycle and he had only - 10 - learner's licence.
On the contrary, deceased pillion rider had also no licence to ride two wheeler.
Hence, the requirement of Central Motor Vehicle Act was not complied and hence, it is breach of condition of the policy of insurance by the owner of the motorcycle.
Hence, appellant is not liable to pay the compensation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
While deciding the matter or settling the matters before the Lok Adalath, table of notional income is prepared and according to the said table, if any accident had taken place during 2012,
notional income of the victim or deceased who died in the accident, is taken as Rs.6,500/- p.m. and The Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160201200/
The deceased had no fixed income.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 1National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others and in the case of 2Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 (2018 SCC Online SC 1546)
Therefore, wife and mother are entitled for compensation under the head loss of consortium.
Accordingly, the petition was maintainable and respondent No.2 i.e., appellant was liable to pay the compensation.
The said finding is on the basis of law laid down by the superior courts and hence, does not call for any interference.
Therefore, it has a judicial precedent to be followed by the subordinate courts to the Supreme Court.
Hence, the contention of the appellant that the case was registered against an unidentified vehicle,
therefore, appellant is not liable to pay the compensation does not merit consideration.
If rider of the motorcycle had only learner's licence and admittedly, the deceased Babu was a pillion rider had licence to - 16 - drive the light motor vehicle.
The requirement of law is, the person who was sitting as a pillion rider must know the art of driving, so that he can guide the rider of the vehicle.
Admittedly, the deceased had valid driving licence, therefore, it is sufficient compliance of the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act and Rules.
Hence, on that basis also, the appellant cannot disown its liability to pay the compensation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
21. For the aforesaid discussions, we answer the above points accordingly and we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER MFA No.101712/2015 is partly allowed and MFA Cro.100166/2016 is dismissed.
The impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.1530/2012 dated 18.03.2015 is modified.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are directed to pay compensation of The Manager vs Priyanka Wo Babu Muntelkar on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160201200/
9 Rs.14,31,472/- as against Rs.16,37,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
As rightly held by the Tribunal, petitioners are entitled for interest on the said compensation amount at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of the entire amount.
The remaining portion of the impugned  judgment is kept intact.
